notes.title: Update on fixes
notes.content:
On behalf of Big Sugar and HappyGiant, a sincere apology for the issues some of you have experienced on the PC version of Sam & Max: This Time It's Virtual! We worked over the weekend to release a patch which address the most reported issues (mainly for Valve Index users):

- Obstacle Course Issues (Hammer, Wall climbing)
- Bombs Away (screwdriver)

We are working on another patch to address:
- Index controllers alignment
- Teddy Tocks Level issues

We would also advise anyone using Windows Mixed Reality to update their Nvidia drivers (this is a good idea in general). 

If you're experiencing any issues not listed above, please email [b]info@happygiant.com[/b] as they are quick to respond.  

Alternatively, you can leave a bug report here: [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdATC2DVCbsJKvr2yekc1pYo7tvs0Xm-xT6PO39-UrulGE8Xw/viewform]https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdATC2DVCbsJKvr2yekc1pYo7tvs0Xm-xT6PO39-UrulGE8Xw/viewform[/url]

Thank you for patience.

Matt | Big Sugar

notes.title: Sam & Max's VR adventure This Time It's Virtual arrives on Oculus Quest today
notes.content:
Sam & Max: This Time It's Virtual, the wise-cracking anthropomorphic crime-fighting duo's (presumably very silly) plunge into the world of VR, is - after a short delay from its originally announced June launch window - out today on Oculus Quest.

This Time It's Virtual (Sam & Max's first entirely new video game outing since Telltale Games' The Devil's Playhouse in 2010) is the work of developer HappyGiant, which promisingly includes Sam & Max creator Steve Purcell and a number of ex-LucasArts alumni who all worked on the studio's seminal 1993 point-and-click adventure Sam & Max: Hit the Road - writer/designer Mike Stemmle, creative director Mike Levine, and concept artist Peter Chan.

Additionally, David Nowlin and Dave Boat, who've voiced Sam and Max previously in a number of Telltale titles, are reprising their roles as the dubious dog and bunny duo.
